================================================================================ ECommerce Microservices - Testing Guide ================================================================================ Generated: October 4, 2026 Scope: OrderService, InventoryService, PaymentService ================================================================================
PREREQUISITES -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Start all three services before testing:
InventoryService -> http://localhost:5002 PaymentService -> http://localhost:5003 OrderService -> http://localhost:5001
Each service exposes a Swagger UI at its root URL ("/"). Swagger is the easiest way to test interactively, but curl commands are also provided below for scripting / automation.
Note: Azure SQL (serverless tier) databases may take 30-60 seconds to resume from auto-pause on first connection. If a service throws a transient SQL error (40613 "database is not currently available") on startup, simply wait and restart it.
================================================================================ 1. BASIC CRUD ON ORDERS ================================================================================
1.1 Create an Order -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Uses the seeded demo product (aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa, stock = 10).
curl -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/orders \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "customerId": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "items": [ { "productId": "aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa", "quantity": 2, "unitPrice": 500 } ] }'
Expected: 201 Created, body contains { "orderId": "<guid>" }. Copy the returned orderId for the next steps.
1.2 Get an Order -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- curl http://localhost:5001/api/orders/{orderId}
Expected: 200 OK with Id, CustomerId, Status, Total. Expected (unknown id): 404 Not Found.
1.3 Update an Order -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- curl -X PUT http://localhost:5001/api/orders/{orderId} \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "orderId": "{orderId}", "items": [ { "productId": "aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa", "quantity": 3, "unitPrice": 500 } ] }'
Expected: 204 No Content when order is still in Draft status. Note: Since Create() auto-confirms the order, calling Update afterwards is expected to throw "Only draft orders can be updated." This is correct domain behavior, not a bug.
1.4 Delete an Order -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- curl -X DELETE http://localhost:5001/api/orders/{orderId}
Expected: 204 No Content (order + its OrderItems are cascade-deleted). Expected (unknown id): 404 Not Found.
================================================================================ 2. DOMAIN VALIDATION RULES (expect 400 / error responses) ================================================================================
Test Case | Expected Result --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Empty customerId | 400 - "CustomerId is required." Empty items array | 400 - "At least one order item | is required." productId = 00000000-0000-0000-0000-00... | 400 - "Each order item requires | a valid ProductId." quantity <= 0 | DomainException - "Quantity | must be greater than zero." unitPrice <= 0 | DomainException - "Price must | be greater than zero." Update a Confirmed order | DomainException - "Only draft | orders can be updated."
================================================================================ 3. SAGA CHECKOUT FLOW (Inventory + Payment orchestration) ================================================================================
3.1 Happy Path -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Create a fresh order (section 1.1), then call checkout:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/orders/{orderId}/checkout
Expected: 200 OK { "orderId": "...", "status": "Completed", "message": "Inventory reserved and payment processed." }
Verify side effects: - InventoryService: AvailableQuantity for the product decreased by the ordered quantity; ReservedQuantity increased. - PaymentService: a Payment record with status "Processed" exists.
curl http://localhost:5003/api/payments/order/{orderId}
3.2 Payment Failure + Compensation (Saga rollback) -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- PaymentService has a built-in demo rule: any amount >= 99,999 is declined.
Create an order with a large amount:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/orders \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "customerId": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "items": [ { "productId": "aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa", "quantity": 1, "unitPrice": 100000 } ] }'
Then checkout that order:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/orders/{orderId}/checkout
Expected: 503 Service Unavailable { "orderId": "...", "status": "Failed", "message": "..." }
Verify compensation: - InventoryService: the previously reserved stock for this order has been released back to AvailableQuantity (ReservedQuantity decreased again). - This proves the Saga's compensating transaction executed correctly.
================================================================================ 4. RESILIENCE PIPELINE (Retry / Circuit Breaker / Timeout / Rate Limiter) ================================================================================
All outbound HTTP calls from OrderService to InventoryService and PaymentService go through a named resilience pipeline defined in Infrastructure/Resilience/ResiliencePipelineExtensions.cs. Order of execution: Rate Limiter -> Retry -> Circuit Breaker -> Timeout.
4.1 Test Retry -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Steps: 1. Stop PaymentService. 2. Create a new order (section 1.1). 3. Call checkout for that order. 4. Watch OrderService's console output.
Expected console output (exponential backoff with jitter): [Retry] Attempt 2 after ~1000ms due to: ... [Retry] Attempt 3 after ~2000ms due to: ...
After 3 failed attempts, the call ultimately fails and compensation runs (inventory already reserved is released; see section 3.2 pattern).
4.2 Test Circuit Breaker -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Steps: 1. Keep PaymentService stopped. 2. Call checkout repeatedly (8+ times) in a short loop, e.g.:
for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \ -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/orders/{orderId}/checkout done
Expected console output once failure ratio/threshold is exceeded: [CircuitBreaker] Circuit OPENED for 15s.
While open, further calls fail INSTANTLY (no retry delay, fails fast without hitting the network).
3. Wait 15+ seconds, then call checkout once more.
Expected console output: [CircuitBreaker] Circuit HALF-OPEN - testing downstream with a trial request.
4. Restart PaymentService, then call checkout again.
Expected console output: [CircuitBreaker] Circuit CLOSED - downstream recovered.
4.3 Test Timeout -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Per-attempt timeout is configured at 5 seconds. This is hard to trigger without an artificially slow downstream service. To verify the mechanism works, temporarily lower the Timeout value in ResiliencePipelineExtensions.cs (e.g., to 1 millisecond), restart OrderService, and call checkout.
Expected console output: [Timeout] Request exceeded 0.001s and was aborted.
Remember to revert the timeout value back afterwards.
4.4 Test Rate Limiting -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The pipeline allows 10 concurrent requests with a queue of 20 more before rejecting. Fire a burst of concurrent checkout calls to exceed this limit, e.g.:
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \ -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/orders/{orderId}/checkout & done wait
Expected: some requests return 503 due to RateLimiterRejectedException once the permit + queue limits are exceeded.
================================================================================ 5. SWAGGER UI VERIFICATION ================================================================================
Open the following in a browser and confirm each endpoint is listed with correct request/response schemas, and can be executed interactively:
http://localhost:5001/ (OrderService) POST /api/orders GET /api/orders/{id} PUT /api/orders/{id} DELETE /api/orders/{id} POST /api/orders/{id}/checkout
http://localhost:5002/ (InventoryService) POST /api/inventory/reserve POST /api/inventory/release
http://localhost:5003/ (PaymentService) POST /api/payments/process GET /api/payments/order/{orderId}
================================================================================ 6. HEALTH CHECKS ================================================================================
curl http://localhost:5001/health -> {"status":"Healthy","service":"OrderService"} curl http://localhost:5002/health -> {"status":"Healthy","service":"InventoryService"} curl http://localhost:5003/health -> {"status":"Healthy","service":"PaymentService"}
================================================================================ TROUBLESHOOTING NOTES ================================================================================
- "Unable to resolve service for type IInventoryServiceClient" at OrderService startup means the AddHttpClient<...> registrations in Program.cs are missing. Re-add them (see Infrastructure/Resilience/ ResiliencePipelineExtensions.cs and Infrastructure/ExternalServices/).
- Checkout returns 404 "Response status code does not indicate success: 404 (Not Found)" -> InventoryService's /api/inventory/reserve or /release minimal API endpoints are commented out in its Program.cs. Re-enable them.
- "Address already in use" on service startup -> a previous instance is still holding the port. Find and kill it:
lsof -nP -iTCP:5001 -sTCP:LISTEN kill -9 <PID>
- Azure SQL error 40613 "database is not currently available" -> serverless database auto-pause; simply retry starting the service after ~30-60s.
- IMPORTANT: Save/commit working changes to git frequently. Several fixes in this project were lost due to editor/IDE auto-revert of unsaved files. Run: git add -A && git commit -m "working state" after each verified step.
================================================================================ END OF DOCUMENT ================================================================================
